flow.costPlain: Running Snowflake's platform — data centers and the cost of delivering its product and services.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Sales teams and marketing. Up 21% YoY — growing, but slower than revenue.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Building the platform and its AI products. Up 48% YoY — the fastest-growing cost line.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: The back office — finance, legal and admin. Up 19% YoY.

follow100Note: Snowflake spent $142.06 of every $100 it took in on direct and running costs — more than it earned — while other income added $4.04 and tax cost $0.33, leaving a $38.35 loss per $100. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Snowflake reports in thousands (revenue was $828,709K); figures here are shown in $M to three decimals so the lines foot exactly. Excluding stock-based pay and other non-GAAP items, operating income was $36.2M (a 4% margin). Chart note: Snowflake's running costs exceeded its gross profit by $348.6M, other income covered $33.5M of that and tax cost $2.7M, so the chart draws the remaining $317.8M net loss as a 'Covered by cash on hand' source.
oneTimers: $360.4M of stock-based compensation-related charges (including about $21.9M of employer payroll taxes on employee stock transactions), excluded from non-GAAP results.
$23.4M of amortization of acquired intangibles, also excluded from non-GAAP results.
$1.0M of expenses associated with acquisitions and strategic investments, also excluded from non-GAAP results.
otherDetail: Other income of $33.5M, net: $54.8M of interest income on Snowflake's cash and investments, less $21.3M of other expense, net. Income tax was a $2.7M provision. Net loss attributable to Snowflake Inc. was $317.0M (EPS -$0.95), after $0.8M of loss attributable to noncontrolling interests.

segments.name: Product
segments.note: Customers pay to store data and run computing and AI workloads on Snowflake's platform, billed by how much they use. Up 34% YoY and 95% of all revenue; product gross profit was $569.9M, a 72% margin.

segments.name: Professional services and other
segments.note: Help getting set up and moving data onto Snowflake, plus other small items. Up 17% YoY — but it costs more to deliver than it brings in (a $13.7M gross loss).

sources.label: 10-Q for the quarter ended April 30, 2024 (SEC EDGAR)

takeaways.text: Product revenue rose 34% to $789.6M, the net revenue retention rate was 128%, and remaining performance obligations — work customers have already contracted — grew 46% to $5.0B. Snowflake guided Q2 FY25 product revenue to $805–$810M, up 26–27%, at a 3% non-GAAP operating margin.
takeaways.title: Product growth stayed strong

takeaways.text: The GAAP operating loss was $348.6M, wider than the $273.2M loss a year ago. The main reason: $360.4M of stock-based compensation-related charges, including about $21.9M of employer payroll taxes on employee stock transactions. Leaving those and similar items out, non-GAAP operating income was $36.2M, a 4% margin (down from 5% a year ago).
takeaways.title: Still a GAAP loss, mostly stock pay

takeaways.text: Snowflake ended the quarter with 485 customers spending over $1M a year on the platform (+30% YoY) and 709 Forbes Global 2000 customers (+8% YoY). Operating cash flow was $355.5M and adjusted free cash flow was $365.7M.
takeaways.title: Big customers kept spending

verdict: Snowflake's revenue grew 33% to $828.7M, with product revenue up 34% to $789.6M — but $360.4M of stock-based pay helped leave a GAAP operating loss of $348.6M and a net loss of $317.8M.
